key_insight: Structurally constrained neural softening functions extend pseudo-elastic Mullins models to capture composition-dependent stress softening while preserving physical admissibility.
engineering_relevance: The approach could improve constitutive predictions and calibration reliability for rubber components with varying material formulations.
method: Embed parameter-dependent neural softening functions in a pseudo-elastic constitutive framework.
Use multiplicative softening decompositions to satisfy mechanical constraints by construction.
Derive an enforceable sufficient condition for ellipticity and assess flexibility–constraint trade-offs.
evidence_signal: Evaluation uses multiaxial experimental data from carbon black-filled EPDM rubber with varying curative amounts to assess prediction accuracy and calibration robustness.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative performance gains or evidence of generalization beyond the studied EPDM formulations.
paper_title: Constrained neural softening functions for the Mullins effect in parameter-dependent materials
